english.title: Owner of unlicensed public hackney carriage cause it to stand / ply for hire - outside London
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the proprietor of a carriage, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CARRIAGE AND INDEX NUMBER WHERE APPLICABLE..), caused it to stand or ply for hire in

(A)_[a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD AND LOCATION..),]_
(B)_[a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..),]_

when it was not licensed as a public hackney carriage
english.legislation: Contrary to section 45 of the Town Police Clauses Act 1847.

english.notes:
(i) The displaying of a sign on a vehicle is not soliciting.
(ii) Courts will take the view that a vehicle plying for hire on private land adjoining a street (e.g. in an adjacent railway forecourt ) with the purpose of attracting customers from that street, is plying for hire in the street (Eastbourne Borough Council v Stirling and Morley 2000).
